c: ClearPath IT Solutions, a managed IT services company for small businesses
j: owner of a dental office (prospective client)
s: ClearPath IT Solutions provides help desk support, cybersecurity and cloud backup. The owner of a five-dentist practice has agreed to a meeting. He is happy with his current part-time IT contractor but worries about a ransomware attack.
You will meet with the prospect (judge) to learn about his needs and present how ClearPath can help. He is concerned about cost and about patient privacy.
p: Explain the selling process
Determine customer/client needs
Analyze product information to identify product features and benefits
Convert customer/client objections into selling points
Explain legal and ethical considerations in selling
n: Opens with questions about his current setup, risks and goals
Ties services to benefits: fewer outages, protection of patient records, predictable cost
Responds to the cost concern by comparing it to downtime or breach cost
Does not exaggerate security promises and mentions privacy obligations
q: 'My contractor is cheaper. Why should I switch?' How do you respond?
What would you do if you realized ClearPath is not the right fit for this client?

c: Spotlight Print & Signs, a local print and signage shop
s: Spotlight Print & Signs relies on walk-in customers. The owner wants to attract local small businesses that need banners, flyers and vehicle graphics, and wants to know how to use social media and email without a large budget.
The owner (judge) wants you to explain which promotional tools fit the shop, how to reach business customers, and how to measure the results.
p: Explain the use of social media for digital marketing
Explain the nature of email marketing tactics
Describe the use of business ethics in promotion
Identify ways to track marketing-communications activities
Explain the nature of direct marketing channels
n: Shares project photos, customer stories and before-and-afters on social platforms
Sends concise emails with an offer and a clear call to action
Honest claims, permission-based lists and respect for unsubscribe requests
Tracks inquiries, coupon codes, website visits and sales by source
q: Which one promotion would you start with, and why?
How would you handle a customer complaint posted publicly on social media?

c: Pinnacle Staffing, which places temporary workers with local businesses
s: Pinnacle Staffing placed a temporary receptionist at a law firm. The firm complained that she arrived late twice and did not understand the phone system. The firm's office manager is threatening to move her business to a competitor.

The client services manager (judge) wants you to explain how to repair this relationship, what a customer service mindset looks like in a business-to-business setting, and how to prevent similar problems.
p: Demonstrate a customer service mindset
Handle difficult customers
Build and maintain relationships with customers
Discuss the nature of customer relationship management
Adapt communication to the cultural and social differences among clients
n: Apologizes sincerely, listens and confirms the issue before proposing a solution
Offers a replacement or additional training and a follow-up call
Keeps notes on client preferences and history in a customer database
Explains how better screening, orientation and check-ins will prevent repeats
q: The office manager says, 'I've lost trust in your company.' What do you say?
How would you check in with clients without being annoying?

c: Brightside Consulting, a firm that helps small businesses grow
s: Brightside Consulting wants to expand into a new market: small restaurants. The managing partner needs to know how many potential clients there are, what restaurant owners need and what competitors charge.
The managing partner (judge) wants you to explain how you would gather information for this decision, which sources are most reliable, and how to turn the findings into a recommendation.
p: Obtain and track information about domestic and foreign suppliers/manufacturers
Determine sources of relevant, new marketing data
Prepare written reports for decision-making
Translate research findings into actionable business recommendations
Explain the principles of data analysis
n: Uses surveys, interviews, trade associations, census and competitor sites
Evaluates reliability, date and sample size of each source
Summarizes findings with clear charts and a recommendation
Links the numbers to a decision: go, wait or adjust
q: What would you do if your research showed the market is too small?
How would you decide between a survey and interviews?

c: Orbit Cleaning Services, a commercial janitorial company
s: Orbit Cleaning Services serves office buildings but is losing clients to competitors that advertise 'green' cleaning. Some of Orbit's best customers have asked about eco-friendly options.
The vice president (judge) wants you to explain how Orbit could develop a new service, how to position it against competitors, and how to price and package it.
p: Explain new product-development processes
Develop positioning concept for a new product idea
Identify product's/service's competitive advantage
Describe the nature of product bundling
Communicate core values of product/service
n: Generates ideas from customer input, tests a pilot and refines it
Positions the service by what it offers, who it serves and why it is better
Identifies advantage such as certified products, trained staff or reliability
Offers packages, for example regular service plus a green add-on
q: How would you test the service before launching it to all clients?
What would you do if customers want green cleaning but are not willing to pay more?
